**202. “Rabbi Shimon took him, etc.” Rabbi Shimon took him and kissed him. Rabbi Pineḥas came and kissed him and blessed him, and said: “Certainly, the Holy One, blessed be He, has sent me here. This is the delicate light that I was told was integrated into my house, and which will subsequently illuminate the entire world”** [see section #186#, above]. **Rabbi Elazar replied: “Certainly, fear must not be forgotten in all the commandments, and certainly not in this commandment,** of love; **fear should be attached to it.” How is it attached?** L**ove is good on one side, as it is stated: When He gives him wealth and goodness, long life, children, and sustenance. Then fear should be awakened, that one should fear lest sin causes** [his downfall] and his [fortune] is reversed upon him. **Regarding this it is stated: “Happy is the man who fears always”** [Proverbs 28:14], **since the fear is incorporated in the love.**

**203. “Thus, one should, etc.” Thus, one should awaken the fear on the other side of harsh judgment: When one sees that a harsh judgment rests upon him, he should awaken the fear and fear his Master appropriately, and not harden his heart. With regard to this, it is stated: “He who hardens his heart will fall into evil”** [Proverbs 28:14], meaning that he will fall **to that other side, which is called “evil.” The result is that fear holds onto both sides,** the side of good and love and the side of harsh judgment, **and is incorporated in them. If the fear incorporates the side of good and love, it is an appropriate whole love.**

Explanation: Fear is a commandment that incorporates all of the commandments of the Torah, since it is the gate to faith in God. In accordance with the awakening of one’s fear, so will the faith in His providence reside upon [the person], as stated above. Consequently, **“this fear must not be forgotten in all the commandments”** [section #202#] – one must not forget the **fear** in each and every commandment, **“much less in this commandment,”** especially with regard to the commandment of **love,** i. e., fear must be awakened along with it. This is because it is in the commandment of love that fear is actually united together with [love], as stated. Accordingly, one must awaken the fear on **both sides** of the **love,** both **love “in mercy and the success of one’s ways”** [section #201#] and **love** at a time of **harsh judgment,** as [the Zohar ] proceeds to explain.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Fear should be attached to it. How is it attached? Love** [etc.,” section #202#]. [The Zohar ] is taking care that we will not err in its words, with regard to its statement that complete **love** is when He takes one’s soul, i. e., at a time of **harsh judgment.** We [might] think that the meaning is that we should not be afraid of the harsh judgment at all but only cleave to His love with devotion and without any **fear.** [To counteract this erroneous conclusion, the Zohar ] concludes that **“fear should be attached to it. How is it attached? Love.”** That is, **fear** should also be awakened at that time, just as one awakens the **whole love.**

Here [the Zohar ] reiterates the **two sides** of **love** that were mentioned earlier, i. e., **“whether in judgment or in mercy and the success of one’s ways.”** [The Zohar ] states that one must awaken the **fear on both sides** of **love,** i. e., that at the time of **mercy and success of one’s ways** one must awaken the fear of Him, lest sin [due to lack of fear should manifest and] cause [his downfall] and his love of God cools. [The person should] thus incorporate the **fear** in **love.** Likewise, on the other side of the **love,** at a time of **harsh judgment,** [the person] should awaken the fear of God and not harden his heart or distract his mind from the judgment. He will thus incorporate the **fear** in **love** here as well. If [a person] follows this practice, he will always be in a state of complete **love,** as is appropriate.

With respect to the incorporation of **fear** in **love** on the side of mercy, [the Zohar ] cites the verse: **“Happy is the man who fears always.”** [The Zohar ] expounds the word **“always”** as implying that even when God treats [a person] favorably, he should still fear Him, lest [the lack of fear lead to] sin [which will] cause [his downfall]. Regarding the incorporation of **fear** in **love** on the side of **judgment,** [the Zohar ] quotes the verse: **“He who hardens his heart will fall into evil,”** meaning that one should not harden his heart at a time of judgment for any reason in the world, for then he will fall **“to that other side** [the Sitra Aḥara ]**, which is called ‘evil. ’”** Rather, one must then awaken the **fear** even more, to fear Him and incorporate the **fear** in his whole **love** at that time. Both the first fear and the second fear are not for [the sake of the person's] own benefit, Heaven forbid. Rather, [the person should be] frightened that he might deteriorate in providing satisfaction to his Maker. Understand this well.

The first two commandments have thus been thoroughly clarified. The **first commandment** is fear, and it is a general principle [which incorporates] the whole of Torah and the commandments. It is [referenced in the word] ** Bereshit ,** and it is clarified in the first verse, which is: **“In the beginning** [ Bereshit ] **God created the heavens and the earth.”** In other words, from the **fear,** which is ** reshit **, there emerged **the heavens and the earth,** which are [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba and their offshoots, which are Beria , Yetzira , and Asiya . The second verse is the clarification of the punishment [for violations of the commandment of fear], which are the four death penalties: Tohu is **strangulation;** bohu is **stoning;** “darkness” is **burning,** and “spirit” is **decapitation.**

The **second commandment** is love, which is clarified in the verse: **“And God said, Let there be light** etc.” [This love] contains **two sides:** The first side is in **wealth, long life, children** etc. [section #200#]. The second side is **“with all your soul and with all your might”** [Deuteronomy 6:5], that is, when He takes your **soul** and your **might** the love should be as whole as when He gives you **wealth and long life** etc. In order to reveal this **love,** the light of the act of creation was concealed, and **when it was concealed, the harsh judgment emerged,** as stated above [section #201#]. The **fear** should also be incorporated with the **love** on its **two sides:** On the first side, one should fear lest [the lack of fear lead to] sin [which will] cause [his downfall] and his love will be diminished. On the second side, one should fear the concealment [of the light of creation], which is the judgment to which God sentences him. This is in accordance with the plain meaning of the words of the Zohar .
However, in order to continue onto the rest of the commandments, we must clarify these matters more deeply, [at the level of understanding of] the lofty level of Atzilut .

Know that in the Zohar the four letters of the name ** Havaya ,** which are Ḥokhma , Bina , Tiferet , and Malkhut , are called **fear, love, Torah, and commandment.** The [letter] yod , which is Ḥokhma , is called **fear;** the first [letter] heh , which is Bina , is **love;** the vav is called **Torah;** and the last heh is called **commandment** (as stated in the Zohar , Bereshit , Hashmatot , old editions, page 265a, and in the Zohar , Naso , 37).

[The Zohar ] thus states: **“In the beginning** etc. **This is the first commandment** etc. **This commandment is ‘the fear of God, ’ which is called reshit ”** [see section #189#]. The meaning is as follows: The partzuf of Arikh Anpin is the entirety of the world of Atzilut , which illuminates to all the worlds through its garments, which are called Abba and Imma , Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , and [ Ze'er Anpin ] and Nukba . [ Arikh Anpin ] is also called sealed Ḥokhma , since its Ḥokhma is sealed in its own head and it does not give any of [this Ḥokhma ] to the worlds [below]. Only Bina of Arikh Anpin illuminates to the [lower] worlds.

Therefore, this Bina is called ** reshit ,** since it is the beginning [** reshit **] and the root of all the worlds [below]. It is called **“the fear of God,”** i. e., the fear of sublimity, resulting from **“because He is great and rules, the essence and the root** [of all the worlds], **and everything is considered like nothing before Him”** [section #191#]. From this Bina , [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba emerge, which are called “heavens and earth. " This, then, is how the verse should be understood: **“ Bereshit ,”** with **fear,** “God created heaven and earth,” which are [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba .

This is the meaning of the statement: **“As it is stated: The beginning** [ reshit ] **of wisdom** [ ḥokhma ] **is fear of the Lord** [Psalms 111:10]; **‘the fear of the Lord is the beginning** [ reshit ] **of knowledge** [ da'at ]**’** [Proverbs 1:7], **since this matter is called by the word reshit ”** [see section #189#]. The brains are Ḥokhma , Bina , and Da'at . However, the Ḥokhma of the brains is not the actual Ḥokhma of Arikh Anpin , but only Bina of Arikh Anpin , as stated above. When the Bina of Arikh Anpin ascends to the head of Arikh Anpin , [that Bina ] returns to be Ḥokhma there, and gives Ḥokhma to the partzufim . Thus, the Bina , which is **fear,** is the beginning of Ḥokhma , and this is the meaning of the verse: **“The beginning of wisdom** [ ḥokhma ] **is fear of the Lord**.” Similarly, [fear of the Lord] is the **beginning** of knowledge [ da'at ], because Da'at is the mystical meaning of the root of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , because [ Ze'er Anpin and Nukba ] raise [ Da'at ] to the head of Arikh Anpin to receive Ḥokhma , and therefore [ Ze'er Anpin ] and Nukba also receive Ḥokhma from [ Arikh Anpin ]. This is the meaning of the verse: **“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge** [ da’at ].” The words of the Zohar from here onwards are as explained above.

This is the meaning of the statement: **“The second commandment is a commandment which the commandment of fear holds onto and from which it never departs. It is love”** [section #198#]. Ḥokhma is called **love,** because the [letter] ** yod ** of ** Havaya ** is the mystical meaning of the essence of Bina , i. e., the first three [ sefirot of Bina ], which are Abba and Imma Ila’in , of the aspect of pure air [ avira dakhya ] and the light of Ḥokhma is concealed in them (as stated in section #198# above, fourth paragraph). The place of the revelation of the light of Ḥokhma is from the lower seven [ sefirot ] of Bina , which are called Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , the first ** heh ** of ** Havaya **. For this reason, [that Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna transmit the light of Ḥokhma which is called love, Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna ] are called **love.** This [love] is the **second commandment** after **fear,** because this Ḥokhma is not received from Ḥokhma of Arikh Anpin itself, but from the [ Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna aspect of] Bina , [and Bina is] fear, as stated.

[The Zohar ] says that **the commandment of fear holds onto it and never departs from it.** [This refers to how] the Bina is always united with Ḥokhma and never separates from it. In any place where there is Bina , Ḥokhma is necessarily with it as well, since Ḥokhma and Bina are always attached to one another, and you will never find Ḥokhma without Bina or Bina without Ḥokhma .

[The Zohar ] thereby teaches us that although it was stated that the **first commandment** is **fear,** i. e., Bina , one should not mistakenly think that it is Bina without Ḥokhma . Likewise, regarding the **second commandment,** which is **love, i. e.,** Ḥokhma , one should not mistakenly think that it is Ḥokhma without Bina . Rather, there is Ḥokhma in the **first commandment** as well, and there is also Bina in the **second commandment,** since Ḥokhma and Bina are incorporated and come together, and they never part. However, we name them in accordance with the dominant factor. In the **first commandment,** which is Abba and Imma Ila’in , and the first three [ sefirot ] of Bina , which are the essence of Bina , the dominant factor is Bina , and therefore we call it **fear.** In the **second commandment,** the dominant factor is Ḥokhma , and we therefore call it **love.** Remember this; do not forget it.

This is the meaning of the statement: **“And what is a whole love? This is a great love,** etc. **When it is stated: ‘And God said, Let there be light’** [etc. ]” [see section #198#]. ** Bereshit ** is a sealed utterance, and the main revelation of ** Bereshit ** starts from the verse: “Let there be light,” which is the mystical meaning of the ascent of Bina , which is ** reshit ,** to the head of Arikh Anpin , where it returns to [be] an aspect of Ḥokhma , as stated above. Then Ḥokhma and Bina are together called **“great love.”** This is the mystical meaning of the utterance: “**Let there be light,”** since the Bina ascended to Arikh Anpin and transmits light to all the worlds [below], in the mystical meaning of **great love,** which is Ḥokhma and Bina .

This is the meaning of the statement: **“Love for the Holy One, blessed be He, is interpreted on two sides: There is one who loves Him because he has wealth, long life,** etc.” [section #200#]; **“for one should love the Holy One, blessed be He, as we learned, even if He takes your soul** etc. **Therefore, the light of the act of creation emerged and was subsequently concealed. When it was concealed, the harsh judgment emerged** [section #201#]. The meaning is as follows: It states below ( Bereshit I, page 281, section 352): **“Let there be light for this world, and let there be light for the World-to-Come.”** [God] saw that this world is not fit to be used, and [therefore] He arose and concealed it in the World-to-Come, which is above the diaphragm inside the intestine of [the partzuf of] Arikh Anpin . [In this aspect of Arikh Anpin ] is the aspect of the World-to-Come, [which is] in the place where Abba and Imma Ila’in are positioned, [which are the] first three [ sefirot ] of Bina that end at the chest of Arikh Anpin . [At that place of the chest of Arikh Anpin lies] the diaphragm that separates between the upper waters, Abba and Imma Ila’in , from the lower waters, Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna and [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba . From the chest of Arikh Anpin and below, the light is dimmed and no longer illuminates, and the light is concealed in Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , the lower seven [ sefirot ] of Bina , which are positioned from the chest to the navel of Arikh Anpin , and the light does not illuminate in them.

This illustrates that the Bina was divided into **two sides,** since the light is revealed in the first three [ sefirot of Bina ], which are Abba and Imma Ila’in that are positioned above the chest of Arikh Anpin , in the mystical meaning of the upper waters. One who merits the level of Abba and Imma Ila’in has wealth, long life, children like olive plants around his table [see Psalms 128:3], he rules over his enemies, his ways are established for him, and in whatever he does he shall prosper [Psalms 1:3]. However, the light has already been concealed from the lower seven [ sefirot ] of Bina , which are positioned below the chest of Arikh Anpin , in the mystical meaning of the lower waters. Those who receive from [those lower seven sefirot ] must love God in the aspect of “even if He takes your soul.” This is the mystical meaning of the two sides of **love,** which are the first three and the lower seven [ sefirot ] of Bina , of the aspect of the right [side in Bina ], which is **love.** This [formation of two sides of Bina ] is the result of the concealing of the light of the act of creation. If one merits to be whole in the love of God, both in the **love** of the aspect of Abba and Imma Ila’in and in the love of the aspect of Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , **“this is appropriate love.”**

[The Zohar ] says that one must integrate the **fear** in those two sides of **love.** On the side of Abba and Imma Ila’in **“fear should be awakened, that one should fear lest sin causes** [his downfall]” [section #202#]. In a similar manner, on the side of the love of [the aspect of] Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna **“he should awaken the fear and fear his Master appropriately, and not harden his heart.”** That is, since Ḥokhma and Bina , which are **love** and **fear,** are always attached to one another, the aspect of the Bina , which is **fear,** must be incorporated, [and this refers] both to the first three [ sefirot ] of Bina , which are Abba and Imma Ila'in , and the lower seven [ sefirot ] of Bina , which are Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna .

Then **“the result is that fear holds onto both sides and is incorporated in them. This is the appropriate whole love.”** Here there are two which are four. There is no **love** except [love] with **two sides,** namely the first three and lower seven [ sefirot ] of Bina . Each [of these two aspects of] **love** is incomplete on either one of the two sides unless there is **fear** in each [one] of them. [This incompleteness is because] there cannot possibly be Ḥokhma without Bina , which is **love** without **fear.**

**204. “The third commandment, etc.” The third commandment is to know that there is a great and governing God in the world, and to unify Him every day with an appropriate unification, in the upper six extremities,** Ḥesed , Gevura , Tiferet , Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod , of Ze’er Anpin , **and to render them into one unification with the six words of “Hear O Israel,” and to direct the will upwards with them. Therefore, we must protract** the word **“one”** [ eḥad ] **for the length of six words.**

Explanation: [The Zohar ] is saying two things: 1) One must **know** [that there is a great and governing God in the world]; 2) **“and to unify Him** etc.” First one must **know** those two sides of **love,** which are Abba and Imma Ila’in and Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , as stated above. **“That there is a great God,”** this is Abba and Imma Ila’in , which are mighty and great in [the light of giving]. **“And governing God in the world,”** i. e., Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , which is called “ruler,” indicating the judgments that arise from [ Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna ], as the light was concealed from [ Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna ] and harsh judgment emerged (as stated in the previous section). The terms “ruler” and “governor” denote judgments.

The meaning is that one must know those **two sides** of **love,** and incorporate **fear** in each of them, as stated, and he will [subsequently] receive His love, both **“in mercy and the success of one’s ways”** and **“in judgment”** [section #201#], since [only] then, but not otherwise, is it considered whole **love.** Subsequently, one must **“unify Him every day with an appropriate unification, in the upper six extremities,”** that is, by raising feminine waters to [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , and [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba [ascend] to Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna . Then Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna and [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba ascend and unite as one with **“the upper six extremities,”** which are **[** Abba and Imma Ila’in ]. They are called “the upper **six extremities**” because they enclothe the six extremities of Arikh Anpin . By means of this unification, Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna ascend to the place of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], above the diaphragm of Arikh Anpin . There lies the mystical meaning of the higher waters, and the light is not concealed from [the six extremities of that level]. When [as a result of that ascent] Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna are filled with light, they transmit to [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , and [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba [transmit] to all the worlds [below], and [divine] giving is revealed in the worlds [below]. This is the mystical meaning of **the reading of Shema ,** as stated here.

Now, the six words of **“Hear O Israel”** are the six sides of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba . [The Zohar ] is saying that the six sides of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba must be unified so that they unite as one with the **six upper sides,** which are [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] and Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , as stated just above. [A person] must **“direct the will upwards with them,”** i. e., [when saying Shema , a person must] direct his will and [levels of] nefesh , ruaḥ , and neshama to be incorporated with [these levels of partzufim ] in the aspect of feminine waters.

Therefore, in order to form one unification in the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin , which are **the six words of “Hear O Israel,”** one must prolong the [word] **“one”** [ eḥad ]. That is, one must draw the Ḥokhma in the word ** eḥad .** The light of Ḥokhma , which extends from Ein Sof , blessed be He, to the higher six extremities, which are [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] and Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , unites the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin in the light of Ein Sof . [The word] ** eḥad ** has a numerical value of **thirteen,** which alludes to the drawing of the light of Ḥokhma (as stated in Marot HaSulam , section #2# above; see there). One must therefore have the intention in the ** eḥad ** to draw the Ḥokhma to the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin .

However, in this unification there is no intention to extend [a level of the] first three [ sefirot ] to Ze’er Anpin , but only to expand the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin through their integration in the higher six extremities. [The Zohar ] thus states that **“we must protract eḥad to the length of six words.”** “Protract” [ arkha ] means the drawing of Ḥokhma ; “**to the length of six words,”** means into the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin . The six extremities [of Ze’er Anpin ] thereby become six extremities of maturity, because **the six words** of Shema correspond to the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin . Through this unification, which expands [the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin ] into the six extremities of maturity, it is possible, subsequently, to extend the manifestation of the first three [ sefirot ] to Ze’er Anpin as well.

**205. “This is that which is written, etc.” This is** [the meaning of] **that which is stated: “Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together to one place”** [Genesis 1:9]. This means: **Let the levels under the heavens be gathered into one place, to be in wholeness for six extremities, as is appropriate. And yet, in that unification** of “Hear O Israel,” **one must connect fear to it,** [which means] **that one must protract the** [letter] ** dalet in eḥad ** [“one”]. This is the reason **that the dalet in eḥad is large, and this is** [the meaning of] **that which is stated: “And let the dry land appear”** [Genesis 1:9] – **that the dalet , which is “the dry land,” should appear and be connected to that unification.**

It has already been explained above that the unification of Shema means to draw forth six extremities of maturity. [The Zohar ] thus states: **“This is** [the meaning of] **that which is stated: ‘Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together to one place’; let the levels under the heavens be gathered into one place, to be in wholeness for six extremities, as is appropriate.” “One place”** is the higher six extremities, where the light of Ein Sof , blessed be He, shines in [the form of] the light of Ḥokhma . [The Zohar ] is saying that that **“the levels under the heavens,”** i. e., the **six sides** of Ze’er Anpin , which are **“under”** the Bina and called “heavens” in relation to Ze’er Anpin , will be gathered **“into one place.”** These are the **“six higher sides,** [which will be gathered] **into one place, to be in wholeness for six extremities, as is appropriate,”** so that they too will receive the light of Ḥokhma . Then six extremities of Ze’er Anpin will unite in the proper manner, although only **“in wholeness for six extremities,”** i. e., only [the level of] maturity of six extremities, as stated.

This is the meaning of: **“And yet, in that unification one must connect fear to it,** [which means] **that one must protract the dalet in eḥad .”** This refers to the lower [aspect of] fear, as stated above (section #201#): **“The love that is called whole is that which is on both sides, whether in judgment or in mercy** etc. **Therefore, the light of the act of creation emerged and was subsequently concealed. When it was concealed, the harsh judgment emerged and the two sides were incorporated together, to become whole. This is appropriate love.”** [The Zohar ] subsequently stated (section #202#) that **fear** should be awakened in this **love** as well (see the Sulam on section #202#).

It was explained there that there are two kinds of **love and fear:** Higher **love and fear,** which are called Abba and Imma Ila’in , and lower **love and fear,** which are called Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna . Wholeness is achieved only through both aspects together. Therefore, the light is concealed in Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , in order to reveal the lower **love,** which is even [in a situation] when He takes your soul away; the **fear** must cleave to this lower **love: “And fear his Master appropriately, and not harden his heart”** [section #203#]. Then [the person] will have whole **love and fear,** and he will cleave to Abba and Imma Ila’in and to Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , and receive all the pleasantness and good in them.

This is what [the Zohar ] is saying here, with regard to the unification of the reading of Shema . One first raises the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba and incorporates them in the higher **six sides,** to draw forth the **“great love”** into [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba through the word ** eḥad ,** which is the light that was created on the first day, in the utterance of: “And God said, Let there be light.” **“And yet, in that unification, one must connect fear to it.”** One must also reveal and draw forth the aspect of concealment of this light that was performed in Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , in order [for the person] to become completed with the lower **love and fear** as well, since [without this, one] is not considered whole, as stated. This is the meaning of that statement here, **“that one must protract the dalet in eḥad , that the dalet in eḥad is large,”** as large letters are in Tevuna . Accordingly, **“the dalet in eḥad is large,”** for it alludes to the place of the concealment of the light, which was performed in Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod of [the aspect of] Tevuna [in Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna ]. This is the reason why one must protract it, and direct one’s intent toward [thoughts of] the concealment [of the light] in it. This is in order [that the person] should also cleave to the lower **love and fear,** as [the Zohar ] proceeds to explain.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“‘And let the dry land appear’ – that the dalet , which is ‘the dry land, ’ should appear and connect to that unification.”** There is no wholeness in **the higher love and fear** that were drawn forth through the six words of the reading of the Shema (by means of the word ** eḥad ,** which is the mystical meaning of **“Let there be light”**) without the lower **love and fear**. [This lower love and fear] are revealed by means of the concealment of the light in Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod of [the aspect of] Tevuna [of Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna ], which are called ** dalet ,** as stated. Therefore, after “**Let the waters be gathered together to one place,”** which is the mystical meaning of the drawing forth of light of Ḥokhma to the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin , which are **“under the heavens,”** it is then written: **“And let the dry land appear.”** This is referring to the ** dalet in eḥad ,** that one must **protract it** and have the intention that it should become **dry** through the concealment of the light. This is in order **“that the dalet , which is ‘the dry land, ’ should appear and connect to that unification,”** [i. e., ] that this ** dalet ,** which is the mystical meaning of the [aspect of] Tevuna , should appear and connect **to that unification** of light in Abba and Imma Ila’in , which were drawn forth into the six extremities of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , in order to complete the **love on two sides**, as explained.

**206. “Once it connected there above, etc.” Once** Malkhut **connected there above,** to the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin , **she must be connected below, in her crowds which are the other six edges that are below,** in Malkhut . These are [represented by]: **“Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever,” which contains six other** [Hebrew] **words of unification. Then, that which was “dry land” becomes a land for bearing fruits and offspring, and for planting trees.**

Explanation: After the higher unification through the reading of Shema , in which the ** dalet ** in ** eḥad ** is connected above in [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], that ** dalet ** in ** eḥad ** must be connected to the other six extremities that are below, that is, on the **six sides** of the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin . This is Rachel, who is positioned from the chest of Ze’er Anpin and below, in whom all six hundred thousand souls of Israel are incorporated, called the **crowds** of the Nukba , or “her crowds.”

[The Zohar ] says that after Ze’er Anpin is incorporated in the aspect of light of Abba and Imma Ila’in , and the aspect of concealment of Tevuna is also revealed in [ Ze’er Anpin ] – which is the mystical meaning of **“Let the dry land appear”** [Genesis 1:9] of the ** dalet ** – those two aspects must be drawn forth to the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin which is [positioned] from the chest [of Ze’er Anpin ] and below. This is the mystical meaning of **the six words: Barukh **; ** shem **; ** kevod **; ** malkhuto **; ** le’olam **; ** va’ed ** [“blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever”]. These **six words** correspond to the **six sides,** Ḥesed , Gevura , Tiferet , Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod , of the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin . This is why [the Zohar ] mentions **“blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever,”** since it consists of six other words of unification.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Then, that which was dry land becomes a land for bearing fruits and offspring.”** The meaning is as follows: Previously, [the Zohar ] stated (in section #201#) that in order to [ultimately] reveal **whole love** [that includes] **both sides,** the light **emerged and was subsequently concealed, and when it was concealed the harsh judgment emerged and the two sides were incorporated together.** Thus, the **love** comprised of **both sides** was not completed by concealment alone, but only through **the harsh judgment** that emerged after the concealment.

Accordingly, before **the harsh judgment emerged,** the ** dalet ** in ** eḥad ** was merely **dry land,** without any use whatsoever. [The dalet ] had left its inclusion in the light as a result of the concealment, and the aspect of fear was not [yet] completed in [the dalet ] either, that it could be rectified with lower [aspects of] **love** and fear, which complement the higher [aspects of] **love** and **fear,** since the **harsh judgment,** which is the primary revealing factor of the lower [aspects of] **love** and **fear,** had not yet been revealed.

Now, the place of that harsh judgment is in the heels of Leah, which is in the place of Rachel’s head. [This is because] Ze’er Anpin has two [manifestations of] Nukba : 1) from the chest and above, which is called Leah; 2) from the chest and below, called Rachel. Thus, Leah’s heels, which end at the chest of Ze’er Anpin , touch the head of Rachel, which is positioned from the chest of Ze’er Anpin and below. The presence of the **harsh judgment** is at the end of Leah’s heels, which touch inside the head of Rachel. Consequently, the **harsh judgment** operates only within [the aspect called] Rachel, as no partition and judgment can reveal its influence other than from its placement and below. It follows that the aspect of concealment is completed into [becoming] the level of lower **love** and **fear** only after [this concealment] has been drawn to the place of Rachel, where the **harsh judgment** operates.

This is the meaning of the statement: **“Then, that which was dry land becomes a land for bearing fruits and offspring, and for planting trees.”** That ** dalet ** in ** eḥad ,** which in its place, before the **harsh judgment** was revealed, was **dry land** and a place of desolation unfit for inhabitation, has now, after being drawn to the six extremities of Rachel (which are from the chest of Ze’er Anpin and below), become a fruit-bearing land, suitable for planting trees, i. e., a place of inhabitation. In other words, the lower **love** and fear have been revealed in [this dalet ] in wholeness, complementing the higher [aspect of] love and **fear** so that the love will be on **both sides.** It is only in this manner that all the pleasantness and goodness in Abba and Imma Ila’in can be revealed, as stated above.

[The Zohar ] will then proceed to state [in the next section]: **“And this is** [the meaning of] **that which is stated: ‘And God called the dry land Earth’** [ Eretz ; Genesis 1:10]; **in that unification below,** it became **Earth,** which is **a completed will, as is appropriate.** Eretz is linguistically associated with ratzon [“will”], and it is thus written: **“And God called the dry land Eretz ,”** meaning that He drew forth the ** dalet ** in ** eḥad ** to the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin , to **its six sides,** where the activity of the **harsh judgment** is already revealed. Then the ** dalet **, which was **dry land** and desolate, transforms, in the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin and by means of the pairing of [ Nukba with Ze’er Anpin ], into a fruit-bearing land and a place of inhabitation. In this manner, “God called the dry land **Earth,”** which is **a completed will, as is appropriate,** for the completed will was revealed in [this structure], in the appropriate fashion, and this is **whole love.**

**207. “And this is that which is stated: ‘And God called, ’ etc.” And this is** [the meaning of] **that which is stated: “And God called the dry land Earth** [ Eretz ,” Genesis 1:10]. **In that unification below,** in “blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever,” it became ** Eretz ,** which is **a complete will, as is appropriate.** This is because Eretz is associated with ratzon [“will”]. **Therefore, it is written “it was good,” “it was good,” twice** Genesis 1:10, 12]**: Once for the higher unification, and once for the lower unification. Since** the Malkhut **was unified on both sides,** in the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin and in its own six extremities, **from that point forward: “Let the earth put forth grass”** [Genesis 1:11], **for she was established to bear fruits and offspring properly.**

Explanation: The **higher unification** is the unification of the **six words** of **the reading of Shema .** This [unification] is in the [level of the] large, higher six sides of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], as clarified in the verse: “**Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together to one** [ eḥad ] **place”** [Genesis 1:9]. This unification draws the light that was created on the first day, from the **six sides** of Abba and Imma Ila’in to the six extremities of Ze’er Anpin , as stated. This is the first [instance of] **“it was good”** that was stated regarding the third day of the act of creation [Genesis 1:10].

The **lower unification,** i. e., the unification of the **six words barukh **; ** shem **; ** kevod **; ** malkhuto **; ** le’olam **; ** va’ed ** [“blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever”], is the completion of the ** dalet ** in ** eḥad .** [The dalet ] has no completion other than in the **six sides** of the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin , as stated. This is clarified in the verse: **“And God called the dry land Earth,”** and in the verse: **“Let the earth put forth grass** etc.” [It is] through the six extremities of Nukba that the **dry land** became a fruit-bearing land. It is with regard to this unification of the six extremities of Nukba that [the phrase] **“it was good”** is stated for a second time [Genesis 1:12].

Thus, the first **“it was good”** is for the first unification, and the second **“it was good”** is for the second unification. This is the meaning of the statement: **“Since** the Malkhut **was unified on both sides,”** i. e., **the two sides of love,** by means of the **higher unification** and the **lower unification, “from that point forward: ‘Let the earth put forth grass, ’ for she was established to bear fruits and offspring properly.”** The **lower unification** completes the **love on both sides,** and the lights of Abba and Imma Ila’in are drawn to the six extremities of Nukba , giving **fruits and offspring to** her **masses,** who are the six hundred thousand souls of Israel, [and this] is appropriate.

**208. “The fourth commandment, etc.” The fourth commandment is to know that the Lord, He is God, as it states: “Know this day, and lay it to your heart, that the Lord** [ Havaya ]**, He is God** [ Elohim ,” Deuteronomy 4:39]. That is, **the name Elohim should be incorporated in the name Havaya , to know that they are one and there is no separation between them.**

Explanation: ** Havaya ** is Ze’er Anpin , while ** Elohim ** is the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin . [The Zohar ] is saying that the Ze’er Anpin and the Nukba must be united without any **separation** between them, i. e., **the name Elohim ,** which is the Nukba , should be incorporated **in the name Havaya ,** which is the Ze’er Anpin , and [then] the Nukba would also be of the aspect of ** Havaya ,** as explained here. This unification is the mystical meaning of the drawing forth of the [level of the] first three [ sefirot ] to [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba . The unification of the reading of Shema , as explained in **the third commandment,** was for the drawing forth of six extremities from [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] to [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , while the unification that is clarified here is for the drawing forth of the first three [ sefirot ] from [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] to [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba . This is the general rule: The drawing forth of any level, whatever it is, cannot be achieved all at once. Rather, first one must draw the six extremities of that level, and afterwards [draw the aspect of] the first three [ sefirot ].

**209. “This is the secret of the verse, etc.” This is the secret of the verse: “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven** […] **to give light upon the earth”** [Genesis 1:14, 15]. This means **that the two names, ** Havaya Elohim , **should be one without any separation at all. The “lights”** [ me’orot ] **without** [the letter] vav , which is the Malkhut that is called Elohim **, will be incorporated in the name “heaven,”** which is Ze’er Anpin , called Havaya , **for they are one and there is no separation in them. A black light,** which is Malkhut , **in white light,** which is Ze’er Anpin : **There is no separation between them and it is all one. This is the white cloud of the day and the cloud of fire of the night.** That is, **the attribute of day,** Ze’er Anpin , **and the attribute of night,** Malkhut , **will be rectified in one another in one unification, to illuminate, as it is stated: “To give light upon the earth.”**

Explanation: The Nukba is called ** me’orot without a vav ,** which represents the diminution of the moon, in accordance with the statement of the Sages that initially the two great lights were on an equal level but the moon complained that two kings cannot use the same crown, and the Holy One, blessed be He, instructed her: “Go and diminish yourself” ( Ḥullin 60b). Then her lower nine descended to the world of Beria and she was diminished to a point under Yesod of Ze’er Anpin . [The Zohar ] is saying that after she was diminished, the Malkhut needs to be incorporated **in the name “heaven,”** which is Ze’er Anpin . That is, [the Malkhut ] must be enlarged once again so that it is a height equal with Ze’er Anpin , face-to-face. The Nukba must be raised back from the world of Beria to Atzilut , and the separation that occurred between the Ze’er Anpin and the Nukba at the time of the diminution of the moon is to be rectified.

The meaning of the diminution of the moon is that the harsh judgment in the heels of Leah ruled over [the Malkhut ], on account of which [the Malkhut ] diminished into a point and its lower nine [ sefirot ] fell into Beria . Now, by means of the unification of the reading of Shema (as stated above, in the third commandment) the Nukba was constructed into [a level of] the six extremities, in the mystical meaning of **the lower unification of “Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever.”** The reason is that through the power of judgment in [the Malkhut ], the ** dalet ** in ** eḥad ** which was **dry land** and desolate, was rectified into **a land** that bears **fruits and offspring** (as stated above [in section #207#]; see there thoroughly).

It now becomes clear that the **black** in the Nukba , which is the force of judgment in her, and which had [caused the Nukba ] to fall to [the level of] a point, is now considered to have ascended to a manifestation of actual light. [The black becomes the light because] it is specifically by the power of the judgment that the ** dalet ** in ** eḥad ** was constructed into an inhabited, fruit-bearing land. Were it not for the force of judgment in the Nukba , the ** dalet ** in ** eḥad **, which is the Tevuna [aspect of Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna ], would remain **dry** and desolate. Thus, the force of judgment in [the Nukba ] becomes actual light. It is called **black light** because the blackness was the cause of this light. It is also regarded as the light of six extremities, which is the light of giving.

Therefore, [after the manifestation of the black light] it is now possible to extend **white light** to the six extremities of Nukba as well, meaning the light of Ḥokhma , which is the [light of the] first three [ sefirot ], since white means Ḥokhma . This is achieved by raising the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba to the palace of Abba and Imma Ila’in . Now the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin can be incorporated with [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] like the Ze’er Anpin , since the force of judgment in [the Nukba ] has transformed into actual light. Even though it is **black light,** [this light] does not act as a barrier at all to prevent the [ Nukba ] from being incorporated in Abba and Imma Ila’in , because **“a black light in white light: There is no separation between them and it is all one.”** Since [this black light] is of the aspect of **light,** [the Nukba ] can be incorporated in the **light** of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], since light in light are a mixture of two [things] of the same kind and are regarded as one. As for the **blackness,** which is the cause of [this black] light, it does not act as a barrier or lower [the Nukba ] now at all, because it is the cause of the elevation [of the Nukba , for without it [the Nukba ] would not be of the aspect of light.

[The Zohar ] thus states: **“This is the white cloud of the day and the cloud of fire of the night; the attribute of day, and the attribute of night.”** In other words, through this unification of the incorporation of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba in [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] – as Ze’er Anpin is incorporated there in Abba Ila’ah and the Nukba in Imma Ila’ah – Ze’er Anpin becomes **a white cloud** for the light of day, and the Nukba **a cloud of fire** for the light of the night. This is **the attribute of day and the attribute of night** that are unified in one another, in the mystical meaning of: **“And there was evening and there was morning, one day”** [Genesis 1:5]. This is the meaning of: **“Will be rectified in one another in one unification, to illuminate, as it is stated: ‘To give light upon the earth. ’” The attribute of day** is incorporated in **the attribute of the night,** which is the Nukba , in the mystical meaning of **“one day,”** and they are rectified in each other to give light upon the earth, to the **crowds** of the Nukba that are in the three worlds of Beria , Yetzira , and Asiya .

**210. “This is the sin of that, etc.” This is the sin of that primordial snake,** which **connects below and separates above. Through this, it caused what it caused to the world. For** [instead] **there must be separating below and connecting above, and the black light,** which is Malkhut , **must be unified above,** in Ze’er Anpin , **in one connection, so that afterwards she will be unified in her hosts in her unification, to separate her from the side of evil.**

Explanation: The unification of the drawing forth of the first three [ sefirot ] to [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba is achieved only by raising [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba to the place of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], above the chest of Arikh Anpin , such that Ze’er Anpin is incorporated in Abba and the Nukba in Imma , and then they both unite. [In that united state, ] the Ze’er Anpin transmits the first three [ sefirot ] from Abba to the Nukba , which is enclothing Imma . Below the chest of Arikh Anpin , however, where the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba are positioned [in this phase], it is forbidden to perform the unification of the drawing forth of the first three [ sefirot ] to Nukba . The reason for this is a lengthy matter, but I will say that this is the sin of the Tree of Knowledge, through which the primordial **snake** brought death to the world. It incited Adam and Eve to perform this unification below, in the place of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , below the chest of Arikh Anpin , and this thereby impaired [the levels] above, as well, stopping the pairing of Abba and Imma Ila’in .

[The Zohar ] thus states: **“This is the sin of that primordial snake,** which **connects below and separates above. Through this, it caused what it caused to the world.”** [The snake] connected the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , for the [purpose of] transmitting the first three [ sefirot ] to the Nukba **below,** in the place [of Ze’er Anpin and Nukba ]. This thereby **caused what** it caused to the inhabitants of the world, i. e., it brought death upon them. This is because it **separated above,** causing the stopping of the pairing of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], from which life is drawn to the inhabitants of the world.

[Explaining further, ] when the Sitra Aḥara approaches to suckle from the pairing that is below the chest of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , which is the place of the hold [of the Sitra Aḥara ], the upper pairing of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] immediately stops, because they are instantly separated from transmitting to each other, so that the shefa [of their pairing] will not descend to the Sitra Aḥara . All of this is because **“it must be separated below and connected above,”** that caution must be taken **to separate** [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba **below** in their place, so that they will not pair with each other down below in drawing forth the first three [ sefirot from above], and **connecting** should only occur **above,** i. e., in the place of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] themselves.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“And the black light must be unified above, in one connection.” The black light,** which is the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin , must be raised with the Ze’er Anpin **above, to the white light,** that is, to [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], and connect the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba there **“in one connection.”** [In this state] Ze’er Anpin transmits the shefa of the first three [ sefirot ] from Abba to the Nukba . After [this], the Nukba returns with the shefa that she received to her place below, where the nefesh , ruaḥ , and neshama of the souls of Israel are located, in [their state of as] aspects of feminine waters.

**“So that afterwards she will be unified in her hosts in her unification” –** [the Nukba ] unites with the souls of the children of Israel, called “the **hosts** of the Nukba ,” in one unification, and transmits to them from the shefa that she received above in the place of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ]. **“To separate her from the evil side,”** because by refraining from connecting the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba [with each other] in their place **below,** the Nukba is separated **from the evil side,** [meaning] that the Sitra Aḥara cannot [receive and] benefit from the shefa . However, if the [ Ze’er Anpin and Nukba are connected **below,** the Sitra Aḥara can receive the shefa , and therefore [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] separate **above** and their pairing is stopped, as stated.

**211. “With all that, one must, etc.” With all that, one must know that Elohim and Havaya ; it is all one, without separation. Havaya is the Elohim ** [Deuteronomy 4:39]. **When a person knows that it is all one, and does not put a separation, even the other side will depart from the world and will not be drawn downward.**

Explanation: “With all that,” that there is such a fear that one might arouse a pairing of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba in their place [below], one should not refrain for this reason from performing the unification in its proper manner, which is in the place of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ]. Instead, **“one must know that Elohim and Havaya ; it is all one, without separation.”** The unification of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba must be drawn forth in the place of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], in order to unite the Ze’er Anpin and Nukba as one, without separation.

**“When a person knows that it is all one, and does not put a separation, even the other side will depart from the world and will not be drawn downward.”** If a person intensifies [his efforts in] the raising of feminine waters and the raising of the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , to unify them in the place of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], as is proper, not only will the ** Sitra Aḥara ** not grasp hold of the shefa , but this will actually cause the removal of the Sitra Aḥara so that it cannot rule over the world.

**212. “This is the secret of the verse, etc.” This is the secret of the verse: “And let them be for lights”** [ me’orot , Genesis 1:15], which consists of the letters of or [light], mot [death]. **For the  kelippa  follows the brain.** The **brain is light,** and the **other side** [ Sitra Aḥara ] **is death. Or is** [spelled out] **in the connected letters** of the word me’orot , whereas ** mot is** [spelled out] **in the separated** letters of the word me’orot . **When this or departs from there, the separated letters of mot connect.** In other words, when you remove the letters of or [ alef ; vav ; resh ] from the word me’orot , the letters of mot [ mem ; vav ; tav ] join together.

Explanation: This is the mystical meaning of the verse: “And let them be for lights.” The kelippa ascends and follows after the brain. Brain is “light,” while the Sitra Aḥara is “death.” ** Or ** [light] is [spelled out] in the connected letters whereas ** mot ** [death] is [spelled out only] in the separated letters. Explanation: the force of judgment in Malkhut is the root of the existence of the Sitra Aḥara and the kelippot , in the mystical meaning of the verse: “And His kingdom rules over all” [Psalms 103:19]. Now, by virtue of the unification of the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba in [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] for the drawing forth of the six extremities and the first three [ sefirot from Abba and Imma Ila’in to Ze’er Anpin and Nukba ], the force of judgment in Malkhut is transformed into **black light,** through the drawing forth of six extremities in the **lower unification** of **the reading of Shema ,** as stated. Subsequently, [ Malkhut ] is raised once more to [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], and the **black light** of Malkhut unites with the **white light** of Abba and Imma Ila’in , as stated above.

Thus, this unification is alluded to in the verse: “And let them be for lights [ me’orot ],” which is the letters of ** or - mot . “ Or is** [spelled out] **in the connected** letters”: By drawing forth the six extremities and the first three [ sefirot ] to the Nukba in **one connection** with the Ze’er Anpin in the place of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], just as the force of judgment was transformed in the Nukba into actual **light** so too all the forces of the Sitra Aḥara and the kelippot that are drawn from this force of judgment are [also] nullified. As a result, **“the  kelippa  follows after the brain,”** [meaning] that the kelippa is nullified because of the power of the brains of the Nukba , since the root of the Sitra Aḥara , which is the force of judgment in the Nukba , was nullified in the **brains** of the Nukba and became light. Accordingly, the force of the kelippa was necessarily nullified as well.

Consequently, **“ or is** [spelled out] **in the connected letters** of the word me’orot , whereas ** mot is** [spelled out only] **in the separated** letters.” By means of the connection of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , through which the force of judgment became **light,** the letters of ** mot ,** which are the Sitra Aḥara , were separated. That is, they were nullified inside the **light** and the combination [of letters spelling out] ** me’orot ** [with the letters of] ** or ** formed in the middle, in the [state of] **connection.** [In contrast, ] ** mot ** is in [a state of] separation, [since] the letter mem is at the start of the word, while the letters vav-tav are at the end of the word.

However, **“when this or departs from there, the letters of the separation, mot , connect.”** In other words, when one does not perform the unification in the place of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], but in the place of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba below, then **“this or departs from there,”** because [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] are immediately separated from their pairing [with each other] and the **light** is stopped. Then the word ** or ** comes out of ** me’orot ** and the result is that **“the letters of the separation, mot , connect.”** [This means that] after the exit of ** or ** from the word ** me’orot **, the word ** mot ** remains there, because the letters of ** or ** have already left the word and they no longer separate between the letters of ** mot .** This alludes to **“the sin of that primordial snake,** which **connects below,”** in the place of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , and therefore **“separates above”** [section #210#] [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], since their pairing stopped because of [the snake] and this brought **death** [ mot ] into the world.

**213. “Eve began from these letters, etc.” Eve’s** [sin] **began from these letters and caused evil to the world, as it is stated: “And the woman saw** [ va’tere ] **that** [the tree] **was good”** [Genesis 3:6]. **She inverted the letters of me’orot ;** that is, she took the letters of va’tere from there, and **there remained** [the letters] ** mem-vav ** from the word me’orot . **They went and took the letter tav with them,** creating the combination mot [death]. **She** [thus] **caused death to the world, as it is stated: “ Va’tere .”**

Explanation: The unification was explained in **the letters of “Let them be me’orot ,”** which are the drawing forth of the first three [ sefirot ] to [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba . When one unifies them above, in the place of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], this draws forth light in **a** [state of] **connection,** for this light] separates **the letters** of ** mot ** as [the light] expands into them, and the combination [of letters spelling the word] ** me’orot ** is formed. But if one unifies [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba below in their place, the light departs once again from the combination ** me’orot ,** leaving ** mot ** there in the connection of the letters (as stated in the previous section above).

[The Zohar ] says [that] **“Eve began from these letters”** because Eve’s sin through the Tree of Knowledge starts with: **And the woman saw** [ va’tere ] **that** [the tree] **was good.”** This alludes [to the idea] that **Eve** drew for herself the letters of **va’tere** from the word ** me’orot ,** i. e., she accepted the advice of the snake to connect [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba in their place below, thereby impairing the combination of ** me’orot .** [In doing so] **“she inverted the letters of me’orot ,”** for by forming a connection below she caused the separation of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] **above.** Thus, the **letters** of the combination ** or ** [ alef-vav-resh ], which separate and negate the combination ** mot ** in the mystical meaning of the word ** me’orot ,** were separated. She formed the combination ** va’tere ,** in which the **letters of or ** are scattered in **inverted** order, because of the ** tav ** that was wedged between them. This ** tav ** is the aspect of the Nukba of the Sitra Aḥara , called ** mot ,** which approached the **light** to receive and suckle from it.

The Sitra Aḥara , which is called ** mot ,** contains male and female: ** Samael ** [“poison”] and **Lilith.** The letter ** mem ** is the male of ** mot ,** called ** Samael ,** while the letter ** tav ** is his female, called **Lilith.** By virtue of [Eve’s] acceptance of the advice of the snake to connect from **below,** the female of ** mot ** immediately approached to suckle from the shefa , and the **letters** of ** or ** were scattered in **inverted** order, as in the combination ** va’tere ,** because the ** tav ** became wedged inside the ** or ** and scattered them.

After **Eve** drew forth the letters ** va’tere ** from ** me’orot , “there remained mem-vav ”** from the word ** me’orot ,** which are the male, called ** mem ** of ** m ** ot , and the expression of Yesod , called ** vav ** of mot . **“They went and took the letter tav with them,”** [meaning] that the male of ** mot , mem-vav ,** which remained from ** m ** e’or**o**t , went to the female, the ** tav ** of mo**t** . The two of them mated and brought ** mot ** upon the world, **“as it is stated: Va’tere ,”** because the male of the Sitra Aḥara , ** mem-vav ,** engaged in a coupling with the ** tav ** of va’**t**ere , who was already in **Eve.** This is the mystical meaning of the snake engaging in relations with Eve and infecting her with contamination [see Shabbat 146a]. By her acceptance of the snake’s advice, the ** tav ** entered her, separating and scattering the letters of ** or ** [ alef-vav-resh ], and forming the combination of the letters ** va’tere ** in her field of vision. Subsequently, the male of the Sitra Aḥara , ** mem-vav ,** came and engaged in a coupling with that ** tav ** which was already in Eve, and ** mot ** [“death”; mem-vav-tav ] appeared in the world.

**214. “ Va’tere . Rabbi Elazar said, etc.”  Va’tere . Rabbi Elazar said: “My father, I learned** that after Eve took the letters va’tere from me’orot , it was not mem-vav that remained, but rather the ** mem alone was left.** For **the vav , which is always a sign of life, was transformed** into mot , death, since **it left and took the tav ** with it, **as it is stated: ‘and she took... and she gave’** [** v**a’**t**ikaḥ …** v**a’**t**iten ; Genesis 3:6]. **This word was** [thereby] **completed and the letters** of mot **joined together.” He replied to him: “Blessed are you, my son.” We have thus established this matter.**

Explanation: Rabbi Eliezer responded [to his father Rabbi Shimon]: We learned that the ** mem ** alone remained, i. e., without the ** vav ,** which is Yesod , because ** Samael ** the male of ** mot ,** had no aspect of Yesod , for a foreign god is infertile. Rather, the ** vav ,** which is always life, that is, the Yesod of holiness, was transformed from holiness into a kelippa and became a Yesod for the male of ** mot .** Subsequently, i. e., after [the male of mot ] had gained the aspect of Yesod from the holiness, ** vav ** went and paired with the ** tav .** Then the ** mem ** was connected with the ** tav ,** by means of the ** vav ** that [the male] stole from the [side of] holiness.

[Rabbi Elazar] cites a proof from the verses dealing with the sin of the Tree of Knowledge, since they begin with a connection of **a vav ** and **a tav , “as it is stated: ‘and she took... and she gave’** [** v ** a’**t**ikaḥ …** v ** a’**t**iten ].” The exit of the ** vav ** to the Sitra Aḥara was born through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge itself [and the Sitra Aḥara lacked the vav ] beforehand. Rabbi Shimon agreed with his point, and **“replied to him: Blessed are you, my son** etc.”

**215. “The fifth commandment, etc.” The fifth commandment. It is stated: “Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures”** [Genesis 1:20]. **There are three commandments in this verse. One is to engage in the Torah;** [the second] **one is to engage in procreation;** [and the third] **one is to circumcise** [a male child] **on the eighth day and to remove the foreskin from there.** One must **engage in the Torah, toil in it every day, to rectify his soul and spirit.**

Explanation: The four previous **commandments,** which are drawn from the first four days of the act of creation, came to rectify the levels in the world of Atzilut itself, which are the four levels Ḥokhma and Bina and [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , in the world of Atzilut . The **first commandment,** which is drawn from the word ** Bereshit ,** is the mystical meaning of **fear,** i. e., supernal Bina . This is the mystical meaning of fear **“because He is great and rules over everything”** [see section #191#]. This [refers] only to the aspect of the first three [ sefirot ] of Bina that was established as Abba and Imma Ila’in , which enclothe Arikh Anpin from the mouth to the chest, called ** yod ** of Havaya .

**The second commandment,** which is drawn from the utterance, **“Let there be light,”** is for the rectification of the lower seven [ sefirot ] of Bina , in the mystical meaning of the **whole, great love,** [and these lower seven are] called Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna . In their main state, [these seven] enclothe Arikh Anpin from the chest to the navel, i. e., below the diaphragm which is inside the intestine of Arikh Anpin . However, in the utterance **“Let there be light,”** which is stated regarding them, they ascended and became one partzuf with [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] above the chest of Arikh Anpin , and from there to the head of Arikh Anpin . The Bina returned to being Ḥokhma there [in the head of Arikh Anpin ], which is the mystical meaning of **great love** and the mystical meaning of the [first letter] ** heh ** of ** H ** avaya . From them, all the brains are transmitted to [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba .

However, from Abba and Imma Ila’in themselves, which are the [aspect of the] first three [ sefirot ] of Bina , [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba cannot receive brains. [This is] because [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] themselves were established in the mystical meaning of “pure air,” which is the light of giving, in the mystical meaning of “because He delights in ḥesed ” [“mercy”; Micah 7:18]. For this reason, [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] are called **“fear,”** because the mystical meaning of **great love,** the brains of the illumination of Ḥokhma , are not transmitted [directly] from [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] to [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , but only from the lower seven [ sefirot ] of Bina , called Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna .

However, the aspect of **great love** in Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna is revealed only from the aspect of the chest of Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna and above, for [those aspects of Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna ] are then positioned above the diaphragm in the intestine of Arikh Anpin . However, from the chest of Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna and below, which are positioned below the diaphragm of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], there is an aspect of concealment of the light of Ḥokhma . This is the mystical meaning of **“Let there be light”** for the next world, which is the Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna above the diaphragm. But the other [aspects of] Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , below the diaphragm, the light was concealed in them and the manifestation of Tevuna in them became the mystical meaning of **dry.**

**The third commandment** is drawn from the two utterances of the third day, which are “**Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together to one place and let the dry land appear”** [Genesis 1:9] and **“Let the earth put forth grass”** [Genesis 1:11]. These are for the rectification of the brains of the six extremities for [ Ze’er Anpin and Nukba . The **upper unification** is drawn from the verse **“Let the waters be gathered,”** which is for Ze’er Anpin , while the **lower unification** is drawn to the six extremities of Nukba from the verse: **“Let the earth put forth grass.”**

**The fourth commandment,** which is drawn from the verse: **“Let there be lights”** [Genesis 1:14], is for the rectification of the first three [ sefirot ] in Ze’er Anpin and Nukba . By the fifth day all the necessary rectifications for [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna , [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba of Atzilut had been rectified, to the point that the [ Ze’er Anpin and Nukba received the [aspect of the] first three [ sefirot ] from [ Abba and Imma Ila’in and Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna ] and [ Ze’er Anpin and Nukba ] were fit for a face-to-face fusion at an equal height [with each other]. Consequently, from here onward, the rest of the commandments are the required rectifications for drawing forth [illuminations] from the face-to-face fusion of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba .

[The Zohar ] thus states: **“The fifth commandment. It is stated: ‘Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures. ’ There are three commandments in this verse.”** The wholeness [resulting from] the mystical meaning of the fusion of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba face-to-face needs to be drawn forth. The first [commandment] is to draw forth a holy soul [that wholeness], so that the person himself will also merit a pure and holy fusion. This is achieved through engagement in the Torah. The second is to birth holy souls, while the third is for the rectification of the sign of the covenant by means of cutting and uncovering [of circumcision], as [the Zohar ] proceeds to explain.

This is the meaning of **“engage in the Torah, toil in it, and add to it** etc.” **“Engage”** means to speak [its words] with [one’s] mouth even if one does not know [its meaning], in the mystical meaning of: “They are life for those who find them” [ motz’eihem ; Proverbs 4:22] – to one who produces [ motzi ] them with the mouth, for he thereby acquires a holy nefesh **“Toil in it”** means to make every effort to do all that one can to grasp it and understand it, for he thereby acquires a holy ruaḥ . **“And add to it”** means that once one has merited to rectify **his soul and spirit,** he should not settle for that, but should always be adding to it, in the mystical meaning of “we elevate in sanctity and do not downgrade” [see e. g., Berakhot 28a]. One thereby merits a holy neshama .

[The Zohar ] continues: **“And add to it every day, to rectify his soul and spirit,”** i. e., increase Torah [study] every day, in order to rectify one’s nefesh and ruaḥ , for by daily adding to the [study of] Torah, and increasing the rectification of his nefesh and ruaḥ , he merits a holy neshama . For **“when a person engages in the Torah, he is rectified with another soul, a holy one”** [see next section], since one who engages in Torah extensively, in addition to meriting a nefesh and ruaḥ , also merits the establishment of a holy neshama .

**216. “The fifth commandment, etc.” When a person engages in the Torah, he is rectified with another soul, a holy one, as it is stated: “With swarms of living** [ nefesh ] **creatures”** [Genesis 1:20]**,”** which means **a soul** [ nefesh ] **from that holy creature,** i. e., Malkhut . **For when a person does not engage in the Torah he does not have a holy soul,** meaning **that the holiness that is above does not rest upon him. But when he does engage in the Torah, through that whisper that he moved in it, he merits a living soul and to be like the holy angels.**

Explanation: “Creature” ( ḥaya ) is the mystical meaning of the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin in the phase [when the Nukba is in a state] of maturity, face-to-face with Ze’er Anpin . In that state, Ze’er Anpin is called **“the tree of life,”** and the Nukba is called **“creature.”** By means of a person’s raising of feminine waters through engaging in the Torah for its own sake and from the coupling of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba face-to-face, [the person] draws forth a holy soul from their fusion. This is the meaning of **“a soul from that holy creature,”** which is the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin . A person attains this only by raising feminine waters through Torah engagement. Thus, **“when a person does not engage in the Torah, he does not have a holy soul,”** for he has no part in the fusion of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Divine Presence, since [the person] did not raise feminine waters to unite them.

This is the meaning of the verse: **“Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures.”** The Torah is called **“water”** [see Bava Kamma 17a], and by swarming with feminine waters, by virtue of the Torah, [a person] merits a holy soul from the supernal ḥaya **.** Know that a person does not merit to cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He, before he attains nefesh , ruaḥ , and neshama from the holy supernal ḥaya (as stated in the Zohar , Vayikra , page 144, section 434). Nefesh is linked to ruaḥ , ruaḥ to neshama , and neshama to the Holy One, blessed be He.

**217. “For it is written, bless, etc.” For it is stated: “Bless the Lord, you, His angels”** [Psalms 103:20]. **These are the ones who engage in the Torah, for they are called “His angels on earth.” This is** [the meaning of] **that which is stated: “And let fowl fly above the earth”** [Genesis 1:20]. **That is in this world,** while **regarding that world we learned that in the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will fashion for them wings like eagles, to roam throughout the world, as it is stated: “But they who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles”** [Isaiah 40:31].

Explanation: It is stated: **“Bless the Lord, you, His angels, mighty in strength, who perform His word, listening to the voice of His word”** [Psalms 103:20]. The Sages explained [the surprising order of] “who perform,” followed by “listening to.” That is, a person typically cannot perform any task before he has heard what his sender has to say to him. This is not the case for the angels; they perform their mission before they hear and understand what God has commanded them. The reason [they function this way] is that the will of God rules over them and there is nothing interposing [between] them [and God] to prevent them from being drawn after God’s will. Consequently, they follow God like a shadow follows a person, so their doing precedes their hearing.

[The Zohar ] says regarding **those who engage in the Torah** and draw forth **a holy soul,** [that] their [physical] substance, although it is from earth, is transformed until it is similar to that of the celestial angels, and [then] their action precedes their hearing. They perform His commandments in total completion [even] before they grasp what they are doing, because they too follow God like a shadow follows a person. This can be compared to the common situation of wind pushing dust into a person’s eyes: He quickly closes his eyelids before his thought can sense it. You will always find in such cases that his action, which is the shutting of his eyes, always precedes his thought’s awareness of the approaching dust.

This is the meaning of the statement: **“His angels. These are the ones who engage in the Torah, for they are called His angels on earth.”** Although they are on earth, their bodies are like that of the celestial angels, and their action precedes their hearing. That is, they do not have to ruminate with their minds before they perform His commandments in fullness, but rather they carry out the commandment in completion before they are able to sense in their thought what they are doing. This is like the shutting of the eyelids, which precedes the deliberation in thought. Consequently, they are regarded as angels on earth.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Wings like eagles, to roam throughout the world, as it is stated: ‘But they who wait for the Lord** etc. ’” “In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will fashion for them wings like eagles, to roam throughout the world.” As long as a person has not merited a holy soul, the Sitra Aḥara rules over him, in the mystical meaning of the verse: **“And the souls of your enemies He will sling out as from the hollow of a sling”** [I Samuel 25:29]. This means (see the Zohar , Vayikra 425) **“that they go and roam the world but find no place to rest, to which they can connect. They become defiled within the side of impurity**... **for they did not enter holiness and were not incorporated in it.”**

The meaning is as follows: It is impossible to cleave to God and fulfill His commandments properly before one believes in the names of the Holy One, blessed be He, that He is good and performs goodness to all, and He is merciful and gracious etc. Those who have not yet merited a soul of holiness are still governed by the Sitra Aḥara . Thus, **“they go and roam the world but find no place to rest.”** When their thoughts roam the world and they see God’s governance over people, they maintain that it is not as good as it ought to be, in accordance with His holy names, [and] they thereby impair the holy names, Heaven forfend. They thus **“find no place to rest,”** where they can believe in His names, **“to connect to Him.”** Consequently, **“they become defiled within the side of impurity,”** meaning that they come to deny Him, Heaven forbid. All this is because **“they did not enter holiness and were not incorporated in it,”** for they did not merit a soul of holiness and did not take [the necessary] actions to be incorporated in holiness.

By contrast, **those who engage in the Torah** and have drawn forth a holy soul, their body is transformed to be like angels, [meaning] that they merit to precede hearing before action, like the [angels]. For this reason it is written about them: “And let fowl fly above the earth,” [i. e., ] that **“the Holy One, blessed be He, will fashion for them wings like eagles, to roam throughout the world.”** This means that they roam the world in their thoughts and perceive God’s governance, and yet not only do they not stumble on **the side of impurity,** but they even receive the strength to raise feminine waters and to increase their power continuously, **“as it is stated: ‘But they who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles. ’”** They thereby mount up **wings as eagles** to roam through all the events of the inhabitants of the world. They are constantly renewing their strength and raising feminine waters through the power of their faith in God’s unity, and they are always drawing forth the spirit of holiness from above.

**218. “This is that which is written, and let fowl, etc.” This is** [the meaning of] **that which is stated: “And let fowl fly above the earth”** [Genesis 1:20]. **The Torah, which is called “water”** [see Bava Kamma 17a], **should swarm and produce the rustle of living creatures; from the place of that creature,** which is Malkhut , **they should draw it below,** as we learned. **With regard to this, David stated: “Create for me a pure heart, O God,” to engage in the Torah, and then: “Renew a steadfast spirit within me”** [Psalms 50:12].

Explanation: Here [the Zohar ] returns to interpret the verse. **“Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures.”** [The Zohar ] states that this **“water”** is **Torah. “Swarm”** means that [the Torah] should produce a living creature nefesh ḥaya , **“from the place of that creature, they should draw it below.”** That is, they should draw this soul [ nefesh ] from the higher Nukba , which is called ḥaya , and from that [ Nukba ], draw [that nefesh ] into this world.

**“With regard to this, David stated: ‘Create for me a pure heart, O God, ’ to engage in the Torah.”** He asked God to give him a pure heart to engage in Torah and to raise feminine waters. **“And then: ‘Renew a steadfast spirit within me, ’”** for he will then merit to draw forth the right spirit and he will be able to cleave to [God, ] blessed be He.

**219. “The sixth commandment, etc.” The sixth commandment is to engage in procreation. Whoever engages in procreation causes that river,** Yesod of Ze’er Anpin , **to be constantly flowing. Its waters will not cease and the sea,** which is Malkhut , **will be filled from all sides. New souls are renewed and emerge from that tree, and many hosts multiply above with those souls,** in order to guard them. **This is the meaning of the verse: “Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures”** [Genesis 1:20]. **This is the sign of the holy covenant, the river that is drawn out and emerges, whose waters multiply and swarm a swarm, and the multiplication of souls for that creature.**

Explanation: Through the awakening from below [a person] awakens [the levels] above, and causes the coupling of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Divine Presence. Then the **river,** which is Yesod of Ze’er Anpin , will be **constantly flowing** with masculine waters [from above to below] and its **waters will not cease** from bestowing upon the Nukba . The **sea,** which is the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin , **will be filled on all sides,** i. e., both from the side of the coupling [needed] to animate the worlds [with divine lifeforce], as well as from the side of bearing souls. “New souls are renewed and emerge from that tree,” that is, not actual new souls, but old souls that were already in Adam the first [man] but which fell from him on account of the sin of the Tree of Knowledge. They are renewed once again by **that tree,** which is Ze’er Anpin , and it is for this reason that they are called “new souls.”

[The Zohar ] continues: **“New souls are renewed.”** Genuinely new souls come to the world only after the completion of the rectification of the sin of the Tree of Knowledge. Many hosts are emanated above with those souls, because **several angels emerge** with each soul, as stated [in the next section] below. Likewise, angels also emerge through the coupling that is for animating the worlds.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“the sign of the holy covenant, the river** etc.” The meaning is [as follows]: **“Swarms of living creatures”** alludes to Yesod of Ze’er Anpin , which is called **“the sign of the holy covenant.”** It is **the river that is drawn out** and emerges from Ze’er Anpin , enclothing the Abba and Imma called Eden, to water the garden, which is the Nukba [of Ze’er Anpin ]. **“Whose waters multiply and swarm a swarm,”** that is, from the couplings of the aspect of six extremities, which are called **“swarms** [ raḥashin ],” which is the Aramaic translation of “Swarm with swarms [ yishretzu sheretz ].” Regarding the aspect of the couplings of the first three [ sefirot ] which is for bearing souls, [the Zohar ] states **“and the multiplication of souls for that creature.”** It is this [creature, the ḥaya , ] that is called **“living creature”** in that verse.
